title: PRD: Compact acceptance matrix for hosted chat/completions/embeddings/rerank + launch checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A compact, testable PRD that unifies behavioral contracts and a minimal launch checklist for hosted API endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Designed to reduce launch friction by codifying required QA scenarios, telemetry gates, and rollback triggers in a concise acceptance matrix.
background: Multiple larger PRDs for hosted endpoints exist, but teams keep redoing similar acceptance criteria and QA. This work creates a lightweight canonical matrix and checklist that product, engineering, and QA can apply to any hosted endpoint launch to improve consistency and speed up readiness decisions.
goals: Provide a 1-page acceptance matrix that covers behavior, performance, security, and degradation handling for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Define concrete telemetry gates and threshold values that must pass in canary traffic before broad rollout
Publish a minimal launch checklist (pre-launch, canary, cutover, post-cutover) that is actionable for PM/Eng/QA/Support
Enable reuse across small incremental endpoint launches to reduce duplicate review cycles
non_goals: Full replacement of existing long-form PRDs or product strategy docs
Specifying internal runtime kernel choices or low-level infra implementation
Designing new client SDKs or breaking API contract changes
requirements: A compact acceptance matrix covering: functional correctness, behavioral consistency vs baseline, latency P50/P95 targets, token-cost regression tolerance, error-rate ceilings, and degradation policy
Telemetry: per-route metrics emitted (requests, tokens, latency P50/P95, error rate, model-fallback count, cache-hit ratio) and dashboards + alert rules documented
QA harness: end-to-end smoke tests and regression prompt set (provided as list of 20 canonical prompts per endpoint) stored in test repo and runnable by CI
Canary policy: traffic slice configuration (min 1% and up to 10%), duration (min 2h), and criteria for promotion/rollback
Acceptance owner: named PM and engineering on-call for canary window
Runbook references: links to rollback steps, cutover scripts, and postmortem template
technical_constraints: Leverage existing hosted runtime routing and canary tooling (no new infra services)
Telemetry must use standard Redwood tags (customer_id, route, model_version, lane)
QA prompt set must be language-agnostic where possible and include edge-case inputs for safety and hallucination checks
acceptance_criteria: Functional: For each endpoint, at least 90% of canonical prompts must produce responses that match the baseline intent classification (tolerance: paraphrase differences allowed)

Performance: P50 latency within target for endpoint tier (chat/completions: P50 <= 180ms for short prompts; embeddings: P50 <= 60ms), P95 tail does not exceed configured SLO (chat/completions: P95 <= 600ms) during canary traffic
Reliability: 99.5% success rate (2xx) for canary slice over 2h, no increase in 5xx errors beyond 0.1 percentage points vs baseline

Cost/Quality regression: token cost per request must not increase by more than 10% vs baseline quantized profile, and quality regression (as measured by eval prompts) must be <= 2% drop in average eval score
Fallback behavior: when model variant not available, automated fallback must return correct routing decision and be accounted in telemetry; fallback percentage must be < 1% during canary
Security: SSO/SAML authorization and KMS key usage validated for Private/Dedicated customers with documented acceptance steps
Observability: Dashboards created and smoke alert firing tested with seeded failing condition (alert must trigger with test payload)
launch_checklist: Pre-launch: finalize PRD and sign-offs from Eng, QA, SecOps, and Solutions (artifact links recorded)
Pre-launch: confirm test suite and canonical prompt set checked into tests/repo and CI pipeline green
Pre-launch: create dashboard and alert links in Console and document SLOs in runbook
Canary: configure 1% traffic slice to canary model/route; run for minimum 2 hours with PM & Eng on-call monitoring
Canary: run full canonical eval suite (20 prompts per endpoint) and compare eval metrics to baseline; document results
Canary gate: if telemetry gates pass, increment slice to 5-10% for at least 4 hours; otherwise, follow rollback runbook
Cutover: execute staged rollout by region and customer-tier (lowest-impact lanes first); validate telemetry after each stage
Post-cutover: run daily regression evals for 7 days and monitor retention of quality metrics
Post-cutover: create launch notes for support, disable canary slice, and convert canary dashboard to historical comparison
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Lab QA: automated CI + unit tests + canary smoke locally
Stage 1 - Small Canary: 1% global traffic (business hours), PM & Eng monitor (2h), automated evals run
Stage 2 - Broad Canary: 5-10% slice (24h aggregate), expanded monitoring, no config changes allowed
Stage 3 - Gradual Cutover: region-by-region roll (5% -> 25% -> 100%), 1 region stabilized before next
Stage 4 - Post-launch Observability: 7-day daily evals, alerts tuned based on observed noise
metrics_and_kpis: Functional accuracy (eval score) vs baseline: target delta >= -2%
Latency: P50/P95 targets by endpoint type
Error rate: total 5xx <= 0.5% during canary; regression delta <= 0.1% vs baseline
Adoption: percent of calls routed to new variant after 7 days
Customer impact: number of support tickets referencing the endpoint in first 7 days
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Spike in tail latency not detected during short canary - Mitigation: extend canary to 24h for high-variance models
Risk: Eval prompt set not representative of real traffic - Mitigation: include sampled production prompt buckets in evaluation and run A/B signal checks
Risk: Increased token cost erodes economics - Mitigation: require cost delta analysis and optional quantized variant under runtime feature flag
Risk: Silent correctness regressions - Mitigation: add human review for low-confidence evals and targeted ABX tests
notes: This compact PRD should be used as the canonical lightweight acceptance contract for small to medium endpoint launches. For large or cross-cutting changes (schema changes, breaking API changes, major model architecture shifts), teams should still author a full PRD and follow the enterprise launch playbook. Review cadence: PM/Eng review scheduled weekly; any acceptance matrix updates must be versioned and linked from the PRD.
